first_party_exceptions.reason: native declared exception: gocritic's ruleguard rules, which are DATA rather than a package any build compiles. No pass reaches it because every pass lints `./...`, and the Go toolchain skips a dot-directory: `go list ./.golangci/...` matches no packages. The dot is deliberate and is what keeps the rules out of every Ze build. It is not unchecked: .golangci.yml points gocritic's ruleguard checker at this exact path with `failOn: all`, so the file is parsed on EVERY pass and a malformed rule stops the run rather than silently dropping every rule in it. What no pass does is run the analyzers OVER it. It stops being blind when a pass can name a package explicitly -- `go list -tags ruleguard ./.golangci/ruleguard` resolves, and the dsl is vendored -- which needs a package selector on Flavor (matrix.go), a field the type does not have because every other flavor is a GOOS, GOARCH and tag set over one fixed pattern

native declared exception: a separate Go module (`module example/acme-monitor`), so `./...` cannot reach it and golangci-lint would need its own run in that directory. It has no tracked go.sum, so the module does not resolve without `go mod tidy`, and this repository vendors its dependencies rather than fetching them. Needs an owner decision on how the example module joins the build

first_party_exceptions.reason: native declared exception: gocritic's ruleguard rules, which are DATA rather than a package any build compiles. No pass reaches it because every pass lints `./...`, and the Go toolchain skips a dot-directory: `go list ./.golangci/...` matches no packages. The dot is deliberate and is what keeps the rules out of every Ze build. It is not unchecked: .golangci.yml points gocritic's ruleguard checker at this exact path with `failOn: all`, so the file is parsed on EVERY pass and a malformed rule stops the run rather than silently dropping every rule in it. What no pass does is run the analyzers OVER it. It stops being blind when a pass can name a package explicitly -- `go list -tags ruleguard ./.golangci/ruleguard` resolves, and the dsl is vendored -- which needs a package selector on Flavor (matrix.go), a field the type does not have because every other flavor is a GOOS, GOARCH and tag set over one fixed pattern

native declared exception: a separate Go module (`module example/acme-monitor`), so `./...` cannot reach it and golangci-lint would need its own run in that directory. It has no tracked go.sum, so the module does not resolve without `go mod tidy`, and this repository vendors its dependencies rather than fetching them. Needs an owner decision on how the example module joins the build

first_party_exceptions.reason: native declared exception: gocritic's ruleguard rules, which are DATA rather than a package any build compiles. No pass reaches it because every pass lints `./...`, and the Go toolchain skips a dot-directory: `go list ./.golangci/...` matches no packages. The dot is deliberate and is what keeps the rules out of every Ze build. It is not unchecked: .golangci.yml points gocritic's ruleguard checker at this exact path with `failOn: all`, so the file is parsed on EVERY pass and a malformed rule stops the run rather than silently dropping every rule in it. What no pass does is run the analyzers OVER it. It stops being blind when a pass can name a package explicitly -- `go list -tags ruleguard ./.golangci/ruleguard` resolves, and the dsl is vendored -- which needs a package selector on Flavor (matrix.go), a field the type does not have because every other flavor is a GOOS, GOARCH and tag set over one fixed pattern

native declared exception: a separate Go module (`module example/acme-monitor`), so `./...` cannot reach it and golangci-lint would need its own run in that directory. It has no tracked go.sum, so the module does not resolve without `go mod tidy`, and this repository vendors its dependencies rather than fetching them. Needs an owner decision on how the example module joins the build
